config.audience: Operations leaders at mid-size logistics companies. Lead with the business outcome; keep it under 400 words.

chunks.text:
# Bluefin Dispatch
Dispatch console and driver app for Bluefin Freight. Replaces the spreadsheet-based morning planning
process with route optimisation, live vehicle tracking and automatic customer notifications.

## Components
- `apps/console` — web dispatch console (Next.js, TypeScript). Drag-and-drop route board, live map.
- `apps/driver` — Flutter driver app for Android and iOS. Proof of delivery with photo and signature,
  offline mode for rural routes.
- `services/api` — NestJS API on PostgreSQL with PostGIS for geospatial queries.
- `services/optimizer` — Python service using Google OR-Tools (vehicle routing with time windows).
- `services/notify` — sends customer ETA messages by SMS and email; message text is drafted by an LLM
  from a fixed template and the live ETA, then checked against the template before sending.

## Infrastructure
Docker images deployed to AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS for PostgreSQL). GPS pings arrive every 30 seconds
from the driver app; positions older than 5 minutes are shown as stale on the map.

## Integrations
- Telematics feed from the existing in-cab units (REST, polled every 60 seconds).
- Accounting export as CSV at the end of each day.

# Discovery notes — Bluefin Freight
Week 1–2 discovery, on site at the main depot.

## How dispatch works today
- Bluefin runs 64 trucks from 3 depots and completes about 340 deliveries per day.
- 5 dispatchers build the next day's routes every morning in three shared spreadsheets.
- Morning planning takes about 2.5 hours; trucks often leave late because routes are not final.
- Drivers get their stops as a printed sheet. Changes during the day go by phone call.
- Customers have no visibility. The office takes around 120 "where is my truck?" calls per day.

## Pain points named by the client
1. Late departures cascade into missed delivery windows (on-time rate 81% last quarter).
2. Empty miles: trucks return to the depot empty on 18% of route kilometres.
3. Dispatchers cannot see where trucks are without calling the driver.
4. Proof of delivery is paper-based; disputes take days to resolve.

## Constraints
- Must keep the existing in-cab telematics units (contract runs until 2027).
- Rural routes have poor coverage, so the driver app has to work offline.
- Go-live before the peak season in October.

# Launch retrospective
## Timeline
- Kickoff 11 February 2025. MVP (console + driver app, manual routing) live at the first depot after 9 weeks.
- Route optimiser and customer notifications added in weeks 10–14; all 3 depots live after 14 weeks.

## What went well
- Pilot at one depot first: drivers gave feedback on the app daily, and 61 of 64 drivers were using it
  within two weeks of the all-depot rollout.
- The optimiser respects customer time windows and driver hours; dispatchers can still drag stops by hand.
- Offline mode: stops, signatures and photos are queued on the phone and synced when the signal returns.

## Numbers after the first full month (September 2025)
- Morning planning is down to about 25 minutes for the whole fleet.
- On-time delivery rate reached 94%.
- Empty-mile share fell to 11% thanks to backhaul suggestions in the optimiser.

## What we would do differently
- Start the telematics integration earlier; the vendor API documentation was incomplete and cost us a week.

[00:00:04] Priya Nair: Thanks for making the time. Can you walk us through a typical morning in dispatch?
[00:00:12] Dana Whitfield: Sure. Every morning we rebuild the same puzzle from scratch in three spreadsheets, and by the time the trucks leave it's already wrong.
[00:00:27] Marco Reyes: And then the phones start. Customers call to ask where their delivery is, drivers call because a stop changed. We spend the day on the phone instead of planning.
[00:00:42] Priya Nair: If this project is a success a year from now, what has changed?
[00:00:56] Dana Whitfield: Trucks leave on time, customers know when we're coming without calling us, and my dispatchers stop being human GPS trackers.
[00:01:13] Marco Reyes: And no more paper. Half our billing disputes are about a signature nobody can find.

[00:00:05] Priya Nair: We pulled the numbers for the first full month after rollout. Want to start with planning time?
[00:00:14] Marco Reyes: Honestly I don't need the report for that. We used to start at six and finish around half past eight. Now it's done before the first coffee.
[00:00:31] Dana Whitfield: The on-time rate is what the board looks at, and it went from 81 to 94 percent.
[00:00:47] Priya Nair: And the customer calls?
[00:00:52] Marco Reyes: Way down. We counted last week and it was about 30 a day, mostly people changing delivery instructions.
[00:01:10] Dana Whitfield: For the first time in years, my dispatchers go home on time and the phones are quiet.
[00:01:24] Priya Nair: Anything that is still not working well?
[00:01:30] Marco Reyes: The accounting export is still a manual step. That's next on our list.
